cites.quote: A cancelled appointment always has a reason of up to 300 characters
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason
Medical history appears only on the patient's own page, never in lists
The column follows the list's `status filter`, date range and paging.
REQ-8 to REQ-10: acceptance criterion 6, split per page.

findings.suggested_fix: Split REQ-6 into three REQs: the column follows the status filter, follows the date range, and follows paging.
findings.text: REQ-6 is compound: it bundles three behaviours (status filter, date range, paging) in one REQ, while AC6 and AC7 were split into one REQ per page and per action.

cites.quote: The full reason is still shown on the appointment's `own page`.

findings.suggested_fix: Mark only glossary terms consistently (Cancelled, Scheduled, Completed, No-show, Dashboard, Medical history) and drop backticks from ordinary phrases.
findings.text: Glossary term marking is inconsistent: No-show is backticked but Scheduled and Completed are not, while non-glossary phrases such as `own page` are backticked as if defined terms.

rubric_items.reason: All 8 acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-15; the 300-char limit and own-page changes are out of scope with reasons; the IDE answer is REQ-16.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable, but REQ-6 bundles status filter, date range and paging, while AC6 and AC7 were split per item.
Every known REQ cites the ticket line or the A-01 IDE answer; nothing invented, no assumed items.
No clash between ticket and baseline; REQ-14 aligns with the data-protection rule and cites both.
The only question (Q-01) was answered in the IDE with real options; no needless open questions.
Readable, but backtick marking of terms is inconsistent and several backticked terms are not glossary terms.
